title: kvx CLI: self-update command and opt-in usage telemetry
context: kvx is an open-source (Apache-2.0) Go CLI for diffing and syncing key/value config across Consul, etcd and AWS SSM, with ~14,000 weekly downloads, distributed via GitHub Releases, Homebrew, and a Debian/RPM repo. Maintainers want users on current versions (two security fixes this year had slow uptake) and want data on which backends are used to prioritise work. Agreed constraints: no new paid infrastructure; nothing collected without explicit user consent. This plan is about to be dispatched to 2 maintainers for a 3-week build.
artifact:
# Plan: kvx self-update + opt-in telemetry

Maintainers: 2 | 3 weeks | Target release: v2.8.0

## 1. Motivation
- After the v2.6.3 credential-logging fix, 41% of release-asset downloads 60 days later were still for versions <= v2.6.2 (GitHub release download counts, tallied per asset).
- Issues #812, #845, #903 ask for "kvx self-update" (78 combined thumbs-up).
- Backend prioritisation is currently guesswork: we maintain 3 backends with equal effort and do not know relative use.

## 2. kvx self-update
Command: kvx self-update [--check] [--version vX.Y.Z]
- Queries the GitHub Releases API for the latest non-prerelease tag; --check only prints whether an update exists.
- Downloads the platform archive and its .minisig signature. The minisign public key is compiled into the binary; the archive is rejected unless the signature verifies. The same key already signs our releases today (documented in SECURITY.md).
- Writes the new binary to a temp file in the same directory, fsyncs, then atomic rename over the current binary. The previous binary is kept as kvx.prev; kvx self-update --rollback swaps them back.
- Package-manager installs: if the binary path is under a Homebrew Cellar or is owned by the dpkg/rpm database, self-update refuses and prints the matching brew/apt/dnf command instead, so we never fight the package manager.
- Startup notice: at most once per 24 h, a single stderr line "kvx vX.Y.Z available (kvx self-update)". Suppressed when stderr is not a TTY, when CI=true, or when KVX_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1. The check is a single HTTPS GET with a 1.5 s timeout run in a goroutine; it never delays the command.

## 3. Telemetry (opt-in)
- Default is OFF. On first interactive run after upgrade, kvx asks once: "Share anonymous usage stats (command name, backend type, kvx version, OS/arch)? [y/N]". Empty answer = no. The prompt is never shown when stdin is not a TTY or CI=true.
- Changeable any time: kvx telemetry on|off|status; KVX_TELEMETRY=0 hard-disables regardless of config.
- Payload (complete list, documented in docs/telemetry.md): command name (e.g. "diff"), backend type ("consul" | "etcd" | "ssm"), exit code class (ok/user-error/internal-error), kvx version, GOOS/GOARCH, and a random install ID generated locally (not derived from hostname, user, or MAC). No arguments, keys, values, paths, hostnames, or endpoints are ever sent.
- kvx telemetry status --show-payload prints the exact JSON that would be sent.
- Transport: batched, at most one POST per day, fire-and-forget with 2 s timeout; failures are dropped, never retried in the foreground.
- Collector: a ~150-line Go service on the project's existing donated VPS, writing daily aggregate counts only (raw events discarded after aggregation). Aggregates are published monthly in the repo under stats/.

## 4. Testing
- Self-update: integration tests against a local fake release server covering valid signature, bad signature, truncated download, non-writable directory, rollback, and the Homebrew/dpkg refusal paths.
- Telemetry: test that nothing is sent when unset, off, CI=true, KVX_TELEMETRY=0, or non-TTY; golden test that the payload schema matches docs/telemetry.md.

## 5. Timeline
- Week 1: self-update (download, verify, atomic replace, rollback) + tests.
- Week 2: package-manager detection, startup notice, telemetry client + consent flow.
- Week 3: collector service, docs/telemetry.md, release notes, v2.8.0-rc1 for 1 week, then v2.8.0.

## 6. Out of scope
- Auto-installing updates without the user running kvx self-update (we only notify).
- Delta/binary-diff updates; full archives are < 12 MB.
- Telemetry for kvx running as a Windows service (no TTY to ask consent); it stays off.

## 7. Success measures
- 60 days after a release, share of downloads on the latest minor version >= 75% (from 59%).
- Telemetry opt-in rate reported transparently in stats/; no target, since it is the user's choice.
decoys: A self-updating binary that downloads and replaces itself looks like a supply-chain / bricking risk, but §2 verifies a minisign signature with a compiled-in key, replaces atomically, keeps kvx.prev with a --rollback command, and refuses on package-manager installs.

Usage telemetry looks like a privacy/consent problem, but §3 makes it default-off with an explicit [y/N] prompt, never prompts in CI/non-TTY, documents the complete payload (no args/keys/values/paths), uses a random local install ID, and keeps only aggregates.
